title: Biological characterisation and comparison of patients with multiple osseous or lymphogenous metastatic carcinomas
summary:
The Poly-CR-P study aims to investigate the extent to which patients with primarily proven bone metastases differ from patients with lymph node metastases with regard to biological characteristics in the tissue (blood, urine and tumour).
For this purpose, blood, urine and tissue will be collected and examined. In the laboratory, tumour cells circulating in the blood and their other biological characteristics as well as other substances present in the blood (proteins, RNA and DNA) will be examined. These parameters will be compared with the tissue of the prostate, squamous cell or renal cell carcinoma and the tissue of any metastases that may be present.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Cohort 1:
• Patients with histologically confirmed prostate carcinoma (adenocarcinoma) 
• Previous local therapy with curative intention
• PSMA-PET-CT for re-staging with evidence of > 5 metastases
• Interdisciplinary tumour board decision with recommendation to change therapy
• No other active tumour disease

Cohort 2:
• Patients with histologically confirmed renal cell carcinoma, bladder cancer, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma or breast cancer.
• Staging with evidence of >/= 2 tumor manifestatations (primary tumor and/or metastases)
• Interdisciplinary tumour board decision with recommendation for therapy
• No other active tumour diseases
Exclusion criteria:
Cohort 1:
• age < 40 yrs
• No consent for study participation
• Histology other than adenocarcinoma

Cohort 2:
• age < 40 yrs
• No consent for study participation
